query: For a multicomponent high-entropy alloy in its high-temperature solid and liquid states, what single intervention could overcome the limited accuracy, availability, and efficiency of determining melting temperature, enthalpy and entropy of fusion, volume change upon melting, and liquid thermodynamic properties across a large compositional space? Formulate one hypothesis that states the intervention and causal mechanism, predicts the outcome relative to current experimental and computational baselines, defines the applicable composition and temperature ranges, identifies supporting prior evidence, and proposes a decisive falsification test against independent reference data.

generation.hypothesis: The intervention of using advanced machine learning models trained on a diverse dataset of high-entropy alloys can accurately predict the melting temperature, enthalpy and entropy of fusion, volume change upon melting, and liquid thermodynamic properties of multicomponent high-entropy alloys across a large compositional space.
generation.material_initial_state: Multicomponent high-entropy alloys in their high-temperature solid and liquid states
generation.intervention: Using advanced machine learning models trained on a diverse dataset of high-entropy alloys
generation.conditions: High-temperature solid and liquid states, various compositional spaces
generation.mechanism: The machine learning models can learn complex patterns and relationships between the composition and properties of high-entropy alloys, allowing for accurate predictions of thermodynamic properties.
generation.predicted_outcome: Accurate predictions of melting temperature, enthalpy and entropy of fusion, volume change upon melting, and liquid thermodynamic properties
generation.boundary: Limited to high-entropy alloys with available data for training and validation
generation.uncertainty: Uncertainty in the accuracy of predictions for alloys with limited or no available data

falsification_experiment.design: Comparison of predicted thermodynamic properties with experimental data for a set of high-entropy alloys
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the predicted properties deviate significantly from the experimental data, the hypothesis is falsified

Question: How does the addition of Cr to the HfMoTaTiZr refractory high-entropy alloy affect its phase composition, microstructure, and room-temperature mechanical properties, specifically regarding the synergy between strength and ductility?. System: HfMoTaTiZr (30.0 at% Hf, 16.1 at% Mo, 30.4 at% Ta, 8.1 at% Ti, 15.4 at% Zr) and HfMoTaTiZrCr0.5 (28.8 at% Hf, 15.5 at% Mo, 29.1 at% Ta, 7.7 at% Ti, 14.7 at% Zr, 4.2 at% Cr). Processing: Vacuum arc melting in an inert gas atmosphere; ingots re-melted at least 5 times to improve chemical homogeneity; weight loss did not exceed 0.5 wt%. Test conditions: Room temperature; Vickers hardness with 0.3 kg load and 15 s dwelling time; compression tests on cylindrical samples (3 mm diameter, 6 mm height) at a ram speed of 0.008 mm s−1 (strain rate 0.001/s). Question: What are the elastic and plastic deformation behaviors of the NbTaTiV refractory high-entropy alloy at room temperature and elevated temperatures, and how do they compare to conventional BCC alloys?. System: Nb23.8Ta25.5Ti24.9V25.8 (nominally Nb25Ta25Ti25V25) BCC refractory high-entropy alloy. Processing: Arc melting under argon atmosphere from 99.99 wt% purity elements, melted 10 times, drop-cast into 4-mm diameter rods, homogenized at 1200°C for 3 days, followed by water cooling. Question: How to determine the elastic constants and derived moduli of a NbTaTiV refractory high-entropy alloy using Resonant Ultrasound Spectroscopy (RUS) across a specific frequency range.. System: NbTaTiV HEA. Test conditions: Cylindrical sample corner-mounted between two transducers; frequency swept through the 100- to 650-kHz range; elastic isotropy assumed.. Findings: Elastic constants C11, C12, and C44 were determined using sample dimensions and observed resonances.; Large responses were detected when the frequency corresponded to an eigenfrequency of the sample.; Bulk modulus (K) and shear modulus (G) were determined using Hill's approximations.. Mechanism: The authors assume elastic isotropy and derive elastic constants from the sample's resonant frequencies and dimensions, then calculate bulk and shear moduli via Hill's approximations.. Quote: "Assuming that the elastic isotropy and the elastic constants, ( C 11 , C 12 , and C 44 ), were determined, using sample dimensions, and observed resonances."

Question: What are the magnetic properties of the as-cast high-entropy alloy FeCoNiTi, specifically regarding the origin of its multiple ferromagnetic transitions and the mechanism behind the high coercive field observed in the fcc phase?. System: FeCoNiTi (equiatomic Fe:Co:Ni:Ti = 1:1:1:1) and a C14-dominant variant Fe27Co27Ni17Ti29. Processing: Arc melting of elemental chips/wires (99.9% purity) in an Ar atmosphere on a water-cooled Cu hearth followed by rapid quenching to produce as-cast polycrystalline samples. Test conditions: DC magnetization measured from 50 to 1150 K under 100 Oe; Isothermal magnetization curves at 50, 100, 200, 300, and 400 K; Electronic structure calculations using CPA with PBE potential. Question: Can a single BCC solid solution of NbMoTaW refractory high-entropy alloy be successfully fabricated via selective laser melting (SLM) despite processing challenges, and how do its microstructure, hardness, and corrosion resistance compare to traditional superalloys and arc-melted counterparts?. System: NbMoTaW refractory high-entropy alloy (nominal equiatomic composition of Nb, Mo, Ta, W powders with 99.9% purity). Processing: Selective laser melting (SLM) using FORWEDO LM120 equipment with a 500 W fiber laser in an argon atmosphere (<20 ppm oxygen); parameters included hatch distance 0.1 mm, layer thickness 0.1 mm, laser power factor 0.8, scanning velocity 250 mm/s, and a triple-pass remelting strategy (3x energy input) to achieve a linear energy density of 2.83 J/mm. Question: How can a nanocrystalline refractory high-entropy alloy (RHEA) film with superior mechanical and tribological properties be synthesized using a cost-effective single target, and what are the effects of annealing on its adhesion and wear performance?. System: Equimolar CuMoTaWV refractory high-entropy alloy (RHEA) film deposited on silicon and 304 stainless-steel substrates. Processing: DC-magnetron sputtering using a single target prepared by partial spark plasma sintering (SPS) of equimolar elemental powders (Cu, Mo, Ta, W, V) at 1000 °C under 40 MPa pressure; film deposition at 500 °C substrate temperature for 120 min in Ar atmosphere (1.16 × 10⁻³ mPa, 150 W power); post-deposition annealing at 300 °C for adhesion improvement. Test conditions: Nanoindentation at 3 mN load; nanopillar compression (440 nm diameter, 3 mN max force); tribological wear tests at room temperature (RT) and 300 °C with 1 N load and 0.1 m/s sliding speed against E52100 alloy steel counterballs.
